title: Fuse dyadic scale and carry streams in reached BIT routes
body:
PR2915 executes a dyadic scale and its adjacent carry as separate complete field passes. This opt-in two-pass affine kernel joins those passes while preserving complete spectator blocks, borrowed sources, distinct output ownership, dirty leases and every native B1 call. It compares against PR3343's already improved direct-carry adapter and leaves standalone scales unchanged.

The 486-bit `A=4,c=-4` kernel costs **163,764 → 55,881** tape operations (65.9% less). A complete ×4 reference route costs **344,457 → 174,573** (49.3% less). The written identity covers `A∈{2,4}`, `|c|≤4`, odd `Q≥3` and inverse maps, with complete `O(BQS+I)` local accounting, at most **17 free scratch roles**, zero numerical words and an unchanged recursive-child recurrence. Component measurements do not imply a multiplication-runtime or κ improvement.

Validation includes 504 exact before/after kernel pairs (37,044 independent columns), six complete route pairs, all 1,123 selected chart types at the explicitly scoped `q=3` identity-low specialization, 16,308 independent fragment cases, 1,152 residue identities and behavioral/source/cost/inventory controls. Raw tiny `c=0` regressions are retained; the adapter preserves standalone scaling. Three alternating fresh-process pairs record timing separately from deterministic certificates.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-affine-streams
```

Expected: all four `PASS_DYADIC_AFFINE_*` checks and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Exact receipts, source pins, proof, validation and open questions are in `research/dyadic-affine-streams/`. Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6; assignment seed 1. Complete enclosing stock/backing, universal native refinement, selected GL64 payload execution and supplier admission remain separate obligations.

Credit Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml for the reached compiler, scaling and native/caller implementation; David Arias for the physical caller; Nick Petalas and Arham Tahir for local cost/countdown work; and the retained PR2157/PR589/PR555 and downstream source lineage. Tekalign/tekuuu, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, source analysis, testing and writing. Apache-2.0; frozen predecessors, upstream and the selected frontier are unchanged.
